testable_competencies.principles: Describe fracture classification terminology (open/closed, displacement, angulation) and the general list of early/late fracture complications (compartment syndrome, infection, malunion/nonunion, AVN, post-traumatic arthritis) that recur across all fracture-specific units.

entries.title: Orthopedic Emergencies (Triage Overview) and Trauma Patient Workup

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The primary/secondary trauma survey and the VON CHOP orthopedic-emergency triage list directly frame objective 109's assess-severity-and-manage-trauma scope, though the disease-specific evidence lives on the individual emergency units below.

testable_competencies.triage: Apply ABCs/primary survey to the orthopedic trauma patient and recognize the finite list of true orthopedic emergencies (vascular compromise, open fracture, cauda equina syndrome, compartment syndrome, hip dislocation, osteomyelitis/septic arthritis, unstable pelvic fracture) requiring immediate action.

entries.mcc_evidence_retention_reason: WEAK/indirect MCC evidence retained (rather than cleared to []) because objective 109's scope genuinely touches this organizing triage content, even though the evidence is not independently sufficient to support DIRECT/COMPONENT classification for this overview-level unit -- the disease-specific evidence lives on the individual emergency units instead.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Open fracture recognition and emergency management (irrigation, IV antibiotics per Gustilo grade, urgent OR) is a paradigm case of objective 109's trauma-management scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match to objective 109-3's diagnose-and-manage bone/joint injury scope for the open-fracture subtype.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize an open fracture as a surgical emergency, apply emergency measures (sterile dressing, splint, IV antibiotics by Gustilo grade, tetanus status, urgent OR for debridement within 6-8 h), and avoid premature wound exploration in the field/ED.

entries.title: Cauda Equina Syndrome

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cauda equina syndrome (saddle anesthesia, bowel/bladder dysfunction, bilateral leg weakness) is a spinal-trauma/spinal-cord-compression surgical emergency directly within objective 109-13's scope.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Back pain and related symptoms (e.g., sciatica)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Presents on a background of severe back pain, within objective 50-4's red-flag-recognition scope for back pain.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize saddle anesthesia, bilateral leg weakness, and new bowel/bladder dysfunction in a patient with back pain as cauda equina syndrome, requiring emergent MRI and surgical decompression.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Neurosurgery's spinal-cord-compression objectives; retained here for the orthopedic back-pain-red-flag recognition angle.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Compartment syndrome is the paradigm limb-threatening complication of bone/joint injury within objective 109-3's complication-recognition scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Compartment syndrome causes vascular/neurovascular compromise, overlapping objective 109-15's vascular-injury scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize pain out of proportion, pain on passive stretch (most sensitive), and a tense swollen compartment as compartment syndrome (a clinical diagnosis) and initiate emergent fasciotomy without waiting for the late '5 Ps'.

entries.title: Osteomyelitis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Osteomyelitis (often post-traumatic or hematogenous) is within objective 109-3's bone-infection-complication scope.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute osteomyelitis presenting as monoarticular-adjacent bone pain overlaps the oligoarthralgia differential.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize fever, bone pain, and elevated inflammatory markers as osteomyelitis requiring blood cultures, imaging, and urgent orthopedic/infectious diseases involvement.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Substantially overlaps Infectious Diseases' bone/joint infection content; retained here for the orthopedic-emergency-recognition angle.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Septic arthritis is a joint-destroying orthopedic emergency within objective 109-3's scope.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute monoarticular joint pain with fever is the classic septic-arthritis presentation within objective 50-1's oligoarthralgia differential.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize acute monoarticular pain, effusion, fever, and inability to bear weight/move the joint as septic arthritis until proven otherwise, obtain joint aspirate before antibiotics when feasible, and initiate emergent IV antibiotics plus surgical drainage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Shoulder (glenohumeral) dislocation, the most commonly dislocated major joint, is a direct match to objective 109-3's joint-injury scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize anterior vs. posterior shoulder dislocation on exam/x-ray, assess axillary nerve and neurovascular status pre- and post-reduction, and perform/recognize indications for closed reduction.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Rotator cuff tendinopathy/tear is a common cause of shoulder-region nonarticular musculoskeletal pain within objective 50-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize rotator cuff impingement/tear on history (painful arc, night pain) and exam (empty can, drop-arm test) and know initial non-operative management versus indications for surgical referral.

entries.title: Acromioclavicular Joint Pathology

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: AC joint sprain/separation presents as localized shoulder-girdle musculoskeletal pain; no dedicated MCC AC-joint objective exists.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize AC joint separation (step deformity, point tenderness) and its grading, distinguishing it from glenohumeral dislocation.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Clavicle fracture, one of the most common adult and pediatric fractures (typically FOOSH/direct shoulder trauma), is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize clavicle fracture clinically and on x-ray, assess for neurovascular (brachial plexus/subclavian vessel) compromise, and know non-operative sling management is standard for most mid-shaft fractures.

entries.title: Frozen Shoulder (Adhesive Capsulitis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Adhesive capsulitis causes progressive shoulder stiffness/pain, overlapping objective 50-3's nonarticular musculoskeletal pain scope; more common in diabetes.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize progressive global shoulder stiffness with a normal x-ray as adhesive capsulitis, especially in diabetic patients, and know management is largely non-operative (physiotherapy, intra-articular steroid).

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Proximal humeral fracture, common in osteoporotic falls in the elderly, is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize proximal humeral fracture on exam/x-ray, assess axillary nerve function, and know most non-displaced fractures are managed non-operatively with early mobilization.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Humeral shaft fracture is the classic cause of radial nerve palsy (wrist drop); direct match to objective 109-11's nerve-injury scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct fracture-management match to objective 109-3.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize humeral shaft fracture as the classic cause of radial nerve injury (wrist drop, sensory loss over dorsal first web space) and document neurovascular status before and after any reduction/splinting.

entries.title: Distal Humeral Fracture

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Distal humeral (supracondylar-adjacent adult) fracture is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize distal humeral fracture and its association with elbow neurovascular injury, requiring careful pre-/post-reduction neurovascular exam.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Supracondylar fracture is the classic pediatric fracture causing anterior interosseous/median nerve or brachial artery injury; direct match to objective 109-11's nerve-injury scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: High risk of brachial artery injury/compartment syndrome (Volkmann's contracture), within objective 109-15's vascular-injury scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Most common pediatric elbow fracture, directly within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize supracondylar fracture as the most common pediatric elbow fracture and the classic cause of brachial artery injury and compartment syndrome (Volkmann's ischemic contracture); perform and document a careful neurovascular exam (radial pulse, AIN/median nerve function) before and after any splinting.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Radial head fracture, the most common elbow fracture in adults (FOOSH), is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize radial head fracture on history/exam (lateral elbow tenderness, painful pronation/supination) and x-ray (sail sign), and know Mason classification broadly guides non-operative versus operative management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Olecranon fracture (direct fall onto point of elbow) is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize olecranon fracture (palpable defect, loss of active extension from triceps avulsion) and know displaced fractures with loss of extensor mechanism require operative fixation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Elbow dislocation (third most common major joint dislocation) is directly within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize elbow dislocation on exam/x-ray (radio-capitellar line), assess neurovascular status, and perform/recognize indications for closed reduction; distinguish simple from complex (fracture-associated) dislocation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Lateral/medial epicondylitis is a classic cause of localized elbow nonarticular musculoskeletal pain within objective 50-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize lateral ('tennis elbow') and medial ('golfer's elbow') epicondylitis clinically and know first-line management is non-operative (rest, bracing, physiotherapy).

entries.title: Elbow Joint Injection (Landmarks)

testable_competencies.procedure: Procedural landmark detail (triangle of lateral epicondyle/radial head/olecranon) for elbow joint injection; a technical procedural skill beyond graduating-medical-student scope.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Forearm shaft fracture-dislocation patterns are within objective 109-3's diagnose-and-manage bone/joint injury scope.

testable_competencies.pattern_recognition: Recognize the 'fracture of necessity' principle (all forearm shaft fractures with joint involvement are operative), and identify the classic eponymous patterns: Monteggia (ulna fracture + radial head dislocation -- always image the elbow), Galeazzi (radius fracture + DRUJ dislocation -- always image the wrist), and isolated ulnar shaft (nightstick) fracture from a direct blow.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Colles' fracture, the most common fracture in patients >40 yr (FOOSH, dorsally displaced distal radius), is a paradigm case of objective 109-3's scope, especially in osteoporotic elderly falls.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize Colles' fracture ('dinner fork' deformity) on exam and x-ray, and know closed reduction with casting is standard for most; consider underlying osteoporosis workup in older patients.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Smith's fracture (volar-displaced distal radius, 'reverse Colles') is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish Smith's fracture (volar displacement, 'garden spade' deformity, typically from a fall onto a flexed wrist) from Colles' fracture (dorsal displacement).

entries.title: Complications of Wrist Fractures

testable_competencies.complications: Recognize early (compartment syndrome, EPL rupture, acute carpal tunnel syndrome) and late (malunion, CRPS, post-traumatic arthritis) complications of distal radius fractures; a reference table rather than an independently testable topic.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Scaphoid fracture (the most commonly injured carpal bone, classic FOOSH with snuffbox tenderness) is a high-yield case of objective 109-3's scope given its AVN risk if missed.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize anatomical snuffbox tenderness after FOOSH as suspicious for scaphoid fracture even with a negative initial x-ray, and immobilize (thumb spica) with repeat imaging in 2 wk to avoid missing an occult fracture and its high avascular-necrosis risk (especially proximal-pole fractures).

entries.title: Wrist and Thumb CMC Joint Arthritis

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Thumb CMC joint osteoarthritis is a common cause of hand/wrist oligoarthralgia within objective 50-1's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize primary/post-traumatic thumb CMC joint arthritis (pain with grind test, z-deformity) and know non-operative management (splinting, activity modification) precedes surgical options.

entries.title: Cervical Spine (Approach, Red Flags, Imaging)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cervical spine anatomy/exam and the differential of neck pain (strain, spondylosis, stenosis, radiculopathy) is within objective 50-5's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Acute cervical spine injury is explicitly redirected in-text to Neurosurgery (NS38); retained here only for the exam/approach angle.

testable_competencies.exam: Apply cervical spine special tests (compression, distraction, Spurling) to localize radiculopathy vs. myelopathy, and recognize which neck-pain presentations require acute-trauma imaging/Neurosurgery involvement.

entries.title: Thoracolumbar Spine (Spondylolisthesis, Low Back Pain Approach)

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Back pain and related symptoms (e.g., sciatica)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Thoracolumbar spine exam (straight leg raise, femoral stretch test) and spondylolisthesis are direct matches to objective 50-4's back-pain-and-sciatica scope.

testable_competencies.exam: Apply straight leg raise and femoral stretch tests to localize lumbosacral radiculopathy, and recognize spondylolisthesis (forward vertebral slip, classically L5-S1) as a cause of mechanical back pain with neurogenic claudication.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Unstable pelvic fracture (a VON CHOP orthopedic emergency) is a direct, high-acuity match to objective 109-3's scope, with major hemorrhage risk.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pelvic fracture is a classic cause of life-threatening pelvic vascular injury/hemorrhage, within objective 109-15's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize unstable pelvic fracture (mechanism, pelvic instability on exam -- performed only once, gently) as a hemorrhage-risk emergency requiring pelvic binder, resuscitation, and urgent orthopedic/trauma team involvement.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Native hip dislocation (usually high-energy trauma, posterior most common) requiring emergent reduction is a direct match to objective 109-3's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Posterior hip dislocation risks sciatic nerve injury, within objective 109-11's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize hip dislocation (classic shortened/internally rotated posterior vs. externally rotated anterior limb position) as an emergency requiring reduction within 6 h to reduce avascular necrosis risk, with sciatic nerve assessment for posterior dislocations.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hip fracture (femoral neck/intertrochanteric), the classic elderly-fall fracture with major morbidity/mortality, is a paradigm case of objective 109-3's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hip fracture is overwhelmingly a consequence of falls in the elderly, directly linking to objective 32's fall-assessment scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize hip fracture (shortened, externally rotated leg, inability to weight-bear) in an elderly fall patient, obtain appropriate imaging (Garden classification for femoral neck fractures), and know that early surgical fixation (<48 h) improves outcomes for most patients.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Hip osteoarthritis (groin/medial thigh pain, decreased internal rotation) is a classic cause of oligoarthralgia within objective 50-1's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Differentiate osteoarthritis (activity-related pain, LOSS x-ray findings) from inflammatory arthritis of the hip (morning stiffness, systemic findings), and know non-operative management precedes arthroplasty.

entries.title: Hip Dislocation Post-Total Hip Arthroplasty

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Post-arthroplasty dislocation is a recognizable acute complication that can present to a generalist/ED setting, though the surgical revision decision-making is specialist-level.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize acute hip pain and leg-length/rotation change after prior total hip arthroplasty as possible prosthetic dislocation requiring urgent orthopedic assessment.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Femoral shaft fracture (high-energy trauma, or pathologic/low-energy in osteoporotic or pediatric patients) is a direct, high-acuity match to objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize femoral shaft fracture (shortened, externally rotated leg, often open injury) as a high-energy trauma requiring hemodynamic assessment (large blood loss potential) and know to rule out an easily-missed ipsilateral femoral neck fracture.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Distal femoral fracture (articular, often elderly fall or high-energy young trauma) is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize distal femoral fracture (knee effusion, extreme pain with motion) and assess for vascular injury (popliteal artery is tethered near the distal femur).

entries.title: Evaluation of the Knee (Exam, Special Tests)

testable_competencies.exam: Perform and interpret core knee special tests (Lachman/anterior drawer for ACL, posterior drawer for PCL, McMurray's for meniscus) that underlie recognition of the specific knee-injury units below.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: ACL/PCL tear (sports/pivoting injury) is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize the audible pop, immediate swelling (hemarthrosis), and giving-way history of an acute ACL tear, and distinguish it from PCL injury (posterior-directed force, e.g. dashboard injury) on mechanism and exam.

entries.title: Collateral Ligament Tears (MCL/LCL)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: MCL/LCL sprain is a common sports-related knee injury within objective 109-3's scope, generally lower-acuity than cruciate/meniscal injury.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize MCL injury (valgus stress mechanism, medial joint line tenderness/laxity) and LCL injury (varus stress), and know most isolated collateral injuries are managed non-operatively.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Meniscal tear (twisting injury, locking/catching) is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize meniscal tear (joint-line tenderness, mechanical locking/catching, positive McMurray's) and know a truly locked knee (fixed extension block) is a surgical emergency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Popliteal (Baker's) cyst is a classic musculoskeletal posterior-knee mass/lump within objective 53's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize a popliteal (Baker's) cyst as usually benign, associated with underlying knee pathology (meniscal tear, OA) in adults, and distinguish it from DVT if it ruptures (pseudothrombophlebitis).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Extensor mechanism (quadriceps/patellar tendon) rupture, causing inability to extend the knee, is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize inability to perform straight leg raise plus a palpable gap as extensor mechanism rupture, and know complete ruptures require early surgical repair.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Knee (tibiofemoral) dislocation carries a high risk of popliteal artery injury requiring emergent vascular assessment, directly within objective 109-15's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Direct match to objective 109-3's joint-injury scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize true knee dislocation as a limb-threatening emergency requiring urgent assessment for popliteal artery injury (ABI, +/- angiography) and peroneal nerve injury, even after spontaneous reduction.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Knee osteoarthritis is one of the most common causes of oligoarthralgia, directly within objective 50-1's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize knee osteoarthritis (chronic joint pain/stiffness/crepitus, LOSS x-ray findings) and know non-operative management (weight loss, exercise, analgesics) precedes surgical referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Patellar fracture (direct impact or indirect extensor-mechanism injury) is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize patellar fracture (inability to extend knee/straight leg raise, palpable deformity) and distinguish it from a benign bipartite patella variant on x-ray.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Patellar dislocation (young, female-predominant, lateral dislocation with apprehension sign) is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize lateral patellar dislocation (positive apprehension test, often self-reducing) in the classic young-female demographic, and know most first-time dislocations are managed non-operatively with closed reduction.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Patellofemoral pain syndrome, a common cause of activity-related anterior knee pain (especially in young athletes), is within objective 50-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize patellofemoral pain syndrome as a common, largely clinical diagnosis of activity-related anterior knee pain managed with non-operative quadriceps/hip strengthening.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Tibial plateau fracture (axial + varus/valgus loading, Schatzker classification) with high risk of concomitant vascular/meniscal injury is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize tibial plateau fracture as carrying risk of compartment syndrome and neurovascular injury (medial fractures especially), and know severe soft tissue injury may delay definitive ORIF.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Tibial shaft fracture (the most commonly fractured long bone) with significant open-fracture/compartment-syndrome risk is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize tibial shaft fracture as carrying a high risk of compartment syndrome (subcutaneous location, tight fascial compartments) and open injury, and know IM nailing is standard operative fixation.

entries.title: Evaluation of Ankle and Foot Complaints

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: The Ottawa Ankle/Foot Rules govern imaging decisions for the ankle-injury cases mapped under objective 109-3 below; this is the organizing exam/imaging-decision unit rather than an independently testable disease entity.

testable_competencies.decision_rule: Apply the Ottawa Ankle and Foot Rules to determine the need for x-ray after acute ankle/foot injury, and perform anterior drawer/talar tilt tests to assess ligamentous stability.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Ankle fracture is a very common presentation directly within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.management: Recognize ankle fracture patterns (Danis-Weber/Lauge-Hansen classification concepts), apply the Ottawa Ankle Rules to guide imaging, and know unstable/displaced fractures require operative fixation while stable fractures may be managed with casting.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Ankle sprain (>90% lateral ligament complex, ATFL most common) is one of the most common musculoskeletal injuries, directly within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.management: Distinguish lateral (inversion, ATFL) from medial/syndesmotic (eversion, deltoid ligament) ankle sprains, grade severity, and know most are managed non-operatively (RICE, functional rehabilitation).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Talar fracture (high-energy axial loading) carries significant AVN risk given the talus's precarious blood supply, within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize talar fracture as a high-energy injury with significant avascular necrosis risk requiring prompt orthopedic referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Calcaneal fracture (classic fall-from-height axial loading injury) is within objective 109-3's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Calcaneal fractures from axial loading (fall from height) warrant screening for concomitant spinal compression fracture, per the same mechanism, within objective 109-13's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize calcaneal fracture after a fall from height, and screen for concomitant lumbar spine compression fracture and contralateral calcaneal/lower extremity injury given the shared axial-loading mechanism.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Achilles tendon rupture (sudden push-off/eccentric loading, positive Thompson test) is a direct match to objective 109-3's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Achilles tendinopathy/tendinitis (overuse, runners) is within objective 50-3's nonarticular musculoskeletal pain scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize acute Achilles tendon rupture (audible pop, palpable gap, positive Thompson test, unable to plantarflex against resistance) versus chronic Achilles tendinopathy, and know functional bracing is a reasonable non-operative option for rupture in low-demand patients.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Plantar fasciitis (classic first-step-in-the-morning heel pain) is a direct match to objective 50-3's nonarticular musculoskeletal pain scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize plantar fasciitis (insidious heel pain worse with first steps after rest, common in runners/obesity/DM) as a clinical diagnosis managed non-operatively (stretching, orthotics, NSAIDs).

entries.title: Bunions (Hallux Valgus)

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize hallux valgus (bunion) as a common, largely cosmetic/degenerative first-MTP deformity managed conservatively (footwear modification) with surgery reserved for refractory pain.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Metatarsal fracture (including the classically nonunion-prone Jones fracture) is within objective 109-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Distinguish a 5th metatarsal avulsion fracture (conservative management) from a Jones fracture (proximal shaft, higher nonunion risk, may need surgical fixation), and apply the Ottawa Foot Rules to guide imaging.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pediatric-specific fracture patterns (greenstick, buckle/torus, plastic deformation from more pliable bone) are within objective 109-3's scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Recognizing fracture patterns inconsistent with the stated mechanism/developmental stage is part of non-accidental-injury screening within objective 74's periodic-health/safety scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize pediatric-specific fracture patterns (greenstick, buckle/torus) due to more pliable bone, and recognize fracture patterns/mechanisms inconsistent with history as a red flag for non-accidental trauma.

entries.title: Stress Fractures

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Stress fractures (repetitive overuse, e.g. in young athletes) are within objective 109-3's scope but represent a lower-acuity chronic-overuse presentation.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize stress fracture (insidious activity-related pain, may be x-ray-occult early) as a repetitive-overuse injury requiring activity modification.

entries.zero_question_reason: Specialist-technique, reference/EBM-summary, or foundational-background content with no independently testable generalist competency identified; not planned for dedicated question coverage at this scope stage.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Growth-plate (physeal) injury and Salter-Harris classification, which determines growth-disturbance risk, is within objective 109-3's pediatric bone-injury scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize physeal (growth plate) injury and know higher Salter-Harris grades carry increasing risk of growth arrest/limb-length discrepancy, warranting orthopedic referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: SCFE (obese adolescent with hip/knee/groin pain and antalgic/Trendelenburg gait) is a classic direct match to objective 20's limp-in-children scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize SCFE in an obese adolescent presenting with hip, groin, thigh, or referred knee pain and a limp/externally-rotated gait, requiring urgent non-weight-bearing status and orthopedic referral to prevent AVN.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: DDH screening (Barlow/Ortolani maneuvers) at newborn/well-child visits is a direct match to objective 74's periodic health encounter/preventive screening scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Undetected DDH presenting later as a limp/leg-length discrepancy overlaps objective 20's limp-in-children scope.

testable_competencies.screening: Perform and interpret Barlow/Ortolani maneuvers on newborn hip screening, recognize risk factors (breech presentation, female, family history, first-born), and know ultrasound is the imaging modality of choice before 6 months of age.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Legg-Calve-Perthes disease (idiopathic avascular necrosis of the femoral head, classically a 4-10 yr old boy with painless or mild-pain limp) is a direct match to objective 20's limp-in-children scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize Legg-Calve-Perthes disease as a cause of insidious hip pain/limp in a young child (peak age 4-10, boys) distinct from SCFE (older, obese adolescent) and transient synovitis (acute, post-viral), requiring x-ray and orthopedic referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Osgood-Schlatter disease (traction apophysitis of the tibial tubercle in active adolescents) is within objective 109-3's overuse-injury scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Presents as activity-related anterior knee pain, overlapping objective 50-3's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize Osgood-Schlatter disease (tender, sometimes prominent tibial tubercle in an active adolescent) as a self-limited traction apophysitis managed with activity modification, not imaging-driven workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Congenital talipes equinovarus is a structural congenital anomaly within objective 36's genetic-concerns scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Recognized on newborn exam as part of periodic health screening.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize club foot on newborn exam (rigid equinus, varus, adduction deformity) and know first-line treatment is serial casting (Ponseti method) initiated shortly after birth.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis screening (Adam's forward bend test) at periodic health encounters is a direct match to objective 74's preventive-screening scope.

testable_competencies.screening: Screen for scoliosis using the Adam's forward bend test, recognize red flags (pain, rapid progression, neurologic symptoms) warranting further workup versus typical adolescent idiopathic scoliosis managed with observation/bracing based on curve magnitude.

entries.title: Benign Active and Aggressive Bone Tumours

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Benign bone tumours (e.g. osteochondroma) presenting as a musculoskeletal lump/mass are within objective 53's scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize benign bone lesion features (well-defined margins, cortex intact, no periosteal reaction) and know most benign active/aggressive lesions require observation or simple curettage rather than oncologic workup.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Malignant bone tumour (primary, e.g. osteosarcoma/Ewing sarcoma in children/adolescents, or metastatic in adults) presenting as a musculoskeletal mass/pain is a direct match to objective 53's scope.

testable_competencies.red_flags: Recognize aggressive imaging features (periosteal reaction, cortical destruction, soft tissue mass) and red-flag history (night pain, weight loss, pain at rest) as suspicious for malignant bone tumour, warranting urgent referral and biopsy before any definitive treatment; recognize that in adults, metastatic disease is a far more common cause of a destructive bone lesion than a primary bone sarcoma.

entries.title: Common Medications (Orthopedic Reference Table)

testable_competencies.reference: Reference table of commonly used orthopedic medications (analgesics, anti-inflammatories, bone-health agents); not an independently testable topic at scope stage.
